body.statement: Let \(B_n\to\infty\) and use exactly the Efron candidate-resampling, strict-feasibility retention, empirical-law output, and zero-retention fallback in the retained-bootstrap definition. Uniformly for \(h\in[0,\bar H]\) under \(P_{n,h}\), \(\sqrt n(\widehat\delta_n-h/\sqrt n)\Rightarrow Z\) with \(Z\sim N(0,4)\), and the ordered endpoints of \(\widehat\Theta_n^{\mathrm{tot}}\) satisfy \(n^{1/4}(\widehat\theta_-^{\mathrm{tot}},\widehat\theta_+^{\mathrm{tot}})\Rightarrow(-\sqrt{(h+Z)_+},\sqrt{(h+Z)_+})\). Conditional on the contact-limit realization, the candidate-retention probability converges to \(\Phi\{(h+Z)/2\}\), whose infimum over \(h\in[0,\bar H]\) is \(\Phi(Z/2)>0\) almost surely. Thus \(B_n\to\infty\) makes the fallback negligible: \(\sup_{h\in[0,\bar H]}P_{n,h}(M_n=0)\to0\). Writing \(\widehat{\mathbb L}_{n,+}^{\mathrm{ret}}\) for the upper-coordinate marginal, the bounded-Lipschitz distance between its pushforward under \(u\mapsto n^{1/4}u\) and \(\mathcal K_h(Z)\) converges to zero in probability uniformly in \(h\); the lower-coordinate marginal converges to the reflected kernel. Centering the retained upper-coordinate law at \(n^{1/4}\widehat\theta_+^{\mathrm{tot}}\) subtracts \(\sqrt{(h+Z)_+}\) from the random kernel.
body.justification: The theorem identifies the fourth-root sampling law and the data-dependent selection kernel of a fully specified finite-sample retained-resampling algorithm, including its asymptotically negligible fallback.
body.gap: It strictly qualifies Watson et al.'s Theorem 4: their differentiability argument omits the square root at \(\delta=0\) and their feasibility filter conditions on a nondegenerate random event.
body.consumer: Users of \(\texttt{leakyIV}\) obtain the correct contact-local reference law and a diagnostic for retained-resample distortion.
body.proof_tex:
Throughout the proof \(h\in[0,\bar H]\), \(a=a_{n,h}\), and all remainders are uniform in \(h\).  The witness-membership theorem gives \(a\to1\), \(\beta=e_1\), \(\alpha=ae_2\), \(\check\theta=0\), and \(\delta=h/\sqrt n\).

Let \(S_n=n^{-1}\sum_iW_iW_i^{\prime}\).  Since the observations are centered Gaussian with uniformly bounded moments,
\[
 \widehat\Sigma_n-\Sigma(a)
 =n^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^n\{W_iW_i^{\prime}-\Sigma(a)\}
   -\overline W_n\overline W_n^{\prime},
 \qquad
 \sqrt n\,\|\overline W_n\overline W_n^{\prime}\|_{\mathrm{op}}=o_P(1). \tag{1}
\]
On the event \(\lambda_{\min}(\widehat\Sigma_{zz,n})\geq m_\Sigma/2\), the resolvent identity gives
\[
 \|R_n(\widehat\Sigma_{zz,n})-
        \widehat\Sigma_{zz,n}^{-1}\|_{\mathrm{op}}
 \leq4m_\Sigma^{-2}n^{-2}. \tag{2}
\]
The fourth-moment expansion for entries of the sample covariance makes the complement of this event \(O(n^{-2})\), uniformly.  Thus (2) is \(o(n^{-1/2})\) for all first-order calculations below.

Differentiate \(\delta=1-\lambda\).  At the witness, the residual in the projection defining \(\lambda\) is \(ae_2\), which is orthogonal to \(\beta=e_1\); hence the derivative of the estimated center drops out and
\[
 \operatorname{IF}_{\delta}(W)=-2aZ_2\epsilon_y. \tag{3}
\]
The smooth covariance expansion based on (1)--(3) gives
\[
 \sqrt n\{\widehat\delta_n-h/\sqrt n\}
 =-2a\,n^{-1/2}\sum_{i=1}^nZ_{2i}\epsilon_{y,i}+o_P(1). \tag{4}
\]
The summands have mean zero, variance one before multiplication by \(-2a\), and uniformly bounded third moments.  Expanding their characteristic functions at the origin therefore gives, uniformly in \(h\),
\[
 \sqrt n\{\widehat\delta_n-h/\sqrt n\}\Rightarrow Z,
 \qquad Z\sim N(0,4). \tag{5}
\]
The center has influence function
\[
 \operatorname{IF}_{\check\theta}(W)
 =Z_1\epsilon_y+aZ_2\epsilon_x,
\]
so \(\widehat{\check\theta}_n=O_P(n^{-1/2})\), while \(\|\widehat\beta_n\|_2=1+O_P(n^{-1/2})\).  The lower truncation \(\|\widehat\beta_n\|_2\vee n^{-1}\) is consequently inactive with probability tending to one.  By the continuous mapping identity \(n^{1/4}\sqrt{(\widehat\delta_n)_+}=\sqrt{(\sqrt n\widehat\delta_n)_+}\), (5) and the definition of the total interval yield
\[
 n^{1/4}(\widehat\theta_-^{\mathrm{tot}},
          \widehat\theta_+^{\mathrm{tot}})
 \Rightarrow
 \left(-\sqrt{(h+Z)_+},\sqrt{(h+Z)_+}\right). \tag{6}
\]

Conditional on the sample, the empirical-bootstrap analogue of (4) is
\[
 \sqrt n(\widehat\delta_{n,b}^*-\widehat\delta_n)
 =n^{-1/2}\sum_{j=1}^n
 \{\widehat\varphi_{I_{bj}^*}-\overline{\widehat\varphi}\}+o_{P^*}(1), \tag{7}
\]
where \(\widehat\varphi_i=-2\widehat a\,Z_{2i}\widehat\epsilon_{y,i}\) is the plug-in version of (3).  The empirical second moment in (7) converges to four and its empirical Lindeberg remainder vanishes, uniformly in \(h\), because the Gaussian witness has moments of every order uniformly on the compact path.  Expanding the conditional characteristic function of the multinomial sum in (7) gives a conditional \(N(0,4)\) limit.  Jointly with (5), it can be represented by \(Z^*\sim N(0,4)\) independent of \(Z\).  Therefore
\[
 \sqrt n\widehat\delta_{n,b}^*\Rightarrow h+Z+Z^* \tag{8}
\]
conditionally on the contact-limit realization.  The bootstrap center is again \(O_{P^*}(n^{-1/2})\), and its bootstrap denominator converges to one.  Hence the scaled candidate upper endpoint converges conditionally to \(\sqrt{(h+Z+Z^*)_+}\), with the lower endpoint its negative.

Strict retention is the event \(\widehat\delta_{n,b}^*>0\).  Because the limiting normal variable in (8) has no mass at zero, its conditional probability converges to
\[
 p_h(Z)=P\{Z^*>-(h+Z)\mid Z\}
 =\Phi\left(\frac{h+Z}{2}\right). \tag{9}
\]
For every realized finite \(Z\),
\[
 \inf_{0\leq h\leq\bar H}p_h(Z)=\Phi(Z/2)>0. \tag{10}
\]
Let \(p_{n,h}\) be the exact conditional candidate-retention probability.  Conditional independence of the \(B_n\) candidates gives
\[
 P(M_n=0\mid W_1,\ldots,W_n)=(1-p_{n,h})^{B_n}. \tag{11}
\]
For any \(\varepsilon>0\), the right side is at most \(e^{-B_n\varepsilon}+\mathbf1\{p_{n,h}<\varepsilon\}\).  Uniform conditional convergence in (9), followed by (10), implies
\[
 \lim_{\varepsilon\downarrow0}\limsup_n
 \sup_{h\in[0,\bar H]}P_{n,h}(p_{n,h}<\varepsilon)=0.
\]
Since \(B_n\to\infty\), (11) proves \(\sup_hP_{n,h}(M_n=0)\to0\).

Finally, for any function \(f\) bounded by one, the conditional variance of the retained empirical average is bounded, on \(p_{n,h}>0\), by a constant times \((B_np_{n,h})^{-1}\).  The preceding small-\(p_{n,h}\) argument shows \(B_np_{n,h}\to\infty\) in probability uniformly.  A finite bounded-Lipschitz net, followed by its Lipschitz extension, therefore turns the conditional ratio law of large numbers into bounded-Lipschitz convergence of the empirical retained law.  Combining this fact with (8)--(9) gives
\[
 \mathcal L\!\left(\sqrt{h+Z+Z^*}\mid
 Z^*>-(h+Z),Z\right)=\mathcal K_h(Z) \tag{12}
\]
for the scaled upper coordinate, and its reflection for the lower coordinate.  Subtracting the original scaled upper endpoint in (6) changes (12) by exactly \(-\sqrt{(h+Z)_+}\).  The zero-retention fallback is negligible by (11), which completes every asserted convergence.
